messages.content: 從一顆距離地球4光年的恆星發出的光需要多少時間才能抵達地球？

function.name: light_travel_time
function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance_in_light_years.description: The distance between the two celestial bodies in light years.

speed_of_light.description: The speed of light in vacuum, in m/s. Default value is 299792458 m/s.

message.content:
從距離地球 4 光年的恆星發出的光，抵達地球所需的時間就是 **4 年**。  
（因為「光年」本身已經是光速在一年內行進的距離，直接把距離除以光速得到的時間正好是光年數。）

But maybe they want to compute using the function? The function calculates time given distance in light years and speed of light. But the distance is already in light years, so the time is distance / (speed_of_light / speed_of_light_in_light_year?). Actually, if distance is in light years, then time in years is just distance. But the function expects distance in light years and speed of light in m/s. It will compute time in seconds? Let's check: The function signature: light_travel_time(distance_in_light_years: number, speed_of_light?: number). It returns any. We need to call the function with distance_in_light_years=4. The speed_of_light default is 299792458 m/s. The function likely calculates time in seconds or maybe in years. But we can compute manually: 1 light year is the distance light travels in one year. So 4 light years is 4 years. So answer: 4 years.
